entries.title: Lighthouse Reef and the Great Blue Hole
paragraphs: This dive follows Lighthouse Reef’s shallow platform and its outer drop-offs around the Great Blue Hole. The sinkhole itself is about 320 m wide and 125 m deep, inside the atoll lagoon.

The terrain grid resolves the atoll’s outer slopes but smooths over the small sinkhole. Its marker records the location; the western limestone alcove is a game addition inspired by drowned cave formations.
The Great Blue Hole and Lighthouse Reef’s Half Moon Caye are protected components of the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

entries.title: Inside the real Blue Hole
paragraphs: The Great Blue Hole is a flooded limestone sinkhole. Stalactites and submerged ledges preserve traces of a cave that formed during lower sea levels and later flooded as the sea rose.
Jacques Cousteau’s Calypso expedition explored it in 1971. A crewed-submarine and sonar expedition in 2018 mapped the interior in much greater detail, including submerged stalactite galleries.
Below roughly 90 m, the lower water is oxygen-depleted and rich in hydrogen sulfide. Reef fish stay in the upper water; the lower sediment still supports microbial life.

entries.title: The reef flat
paragraphs: Lighthouse Reef’s shallow platform stretches for kilometres around the lagoon. Coral, sand and reef rock form a broad shelf before the outer edge falls away into the Caribbean.
Shaped by wave action and slow coral growth over thousands of years, this shallow rim stands in sharp contrast to the sinkhole plunging through its centre.

sources.title: Global Multi-Resolution Topography (GMRT) Synthesis — Ryan et al. 2009, doi:10.1029/2008GC002332

entries.title: Where the atoll ends
paragraphs: A few kilometres east of the hole, the reef flat ends abruptly: this tile's terrain plunges from a few metres deep to nearly 200 m within about half a kilometre, then keeps falling past 3,000 m further out into the open Caribbean. That is the outer wall of the Lighthouse Reef atoll -- a real, steep undersea cliff, and one of the more dramatic features this tile's bathymetry does resolve well.
Beyond the reef edge, the open slope provides a route from sunlit shallows into much darker water.

entries.title: Life on the rim
paragraphs: Caribbean reef sharks, nurse sharks, groupers, squirrelfish and angelfish use Lighthouse Reef’s shallow reef and upper drop-offs.
Reef corals depend on light and belong near the surface. The Blue Hole’s oxygen-depleted lower water excludes reef fish.

entries.title: The western atoll slope
paragraphs: West of the Great Blue Hole, Lighthouse Reef stays almost level for several kilometres before its outer edge drops into deeper water. Along this latitude the mapped seabed is about 2 to 4 m deep over the platform, around 30 m at 87.59° W, 157 m at this scan point, and more than 300 m deep at 87.60° W.
The eastern edge falls away closer to the hole. Scanning both sides shows the width and uneven profile of the atoll platform surrounding the sinkhole.
